category_notes.text: Reviewed reference-style generation, local restoration and image-editing interfaces. Completed guides include native Mac generation and neural collage, with model terms separate from application licenses.

Read controllable image-animation and trajectory-guided video pages, and completed several editable production workflows. Published demonstrations do not prove temporal consistency on arbitrary material.
Reviewed the Neutone package and official FX host, audio-similarity curation, electroacoustic generation and neural DAW candidates. A working host and a usable model are separate requirements.
Revisited neural surface/dynamics research and procedural assembly, and completed Orbia’s scene-consistency evaluation guide. Benchmark geometry is not a ready production asset.

Read NodeTool’s current creative-workspace page and screened local browser studios. The Racik page returned only a shell, so it supplied no substantive new evidence. Local UI and local inference are distinguished.
Read Meta’s agent-assisted immersive-web article and Google’s XR prototyping article. These are primary development contexts, not independent validation of every linked tool.
Reviewed learned media compression and neural fractal/collage representations. Explicit AI authoring is distinguished from the deterministic graphics that an agent creates.
Read biosignal-art and real-time processing descriptions and screened gesture-driven audiovisual tools. Signal-driven interaction is not automatically a learned behavior.
Read current text-to-CAD context and completed KimCad’s beta guide. A simulated printer connector or exported STL does not establish a successful physical print.
Reviewed agent-engine context, sprite automation and neural scene evaluation. Proprietary asset hosts and incomplete platform support remain separate from open adapter licenses.
Read music-to-dance and geometry-conditioned human-motion descriptions. No arbitrary-rig retargeting or live performer test was conducted.
Completed a character-sprite workflow and reviewed virtual-performer context. The xiaoke.ai page is a directory, not evidence of a functioning avatar implementation.
Reviewed video relighting and completed SyncLight’s multi-view lighting guide. Image-view consistency and temporal video stability are different claims.
Read acoustic-field examples and geometry-based sound simulation, alongside stage-position output. Neither a tracking protocol nor a learned field establishes production calibration accuracy.
Read trainable lensless and event-camera reconstruction descriptions. The measurements, sensor and calibration are part of the documented method; none was tested here.
Completed transcript-based editing and broader production guides, while reviewing editable agent-authored film context. Local projects do not establish local transcription or generation.
Completed SVGDreamer and OpenRive guides and revisited SVG reconstruction and editable diagrams. An editable export still needs structural and semantic inspection.
Read the modal kinetic typography page: it still labels code as forthcoming. Screened agent motion parts separately instead of treating a paper demonstration as a released licensed tool.

Completed explanation and film-production guides and screened new short-video authoring interfaces. Factual accuracy, voice quality and source permissions remain unverified unless specifically supported.
Read the OPF toolkit’s editable-deck/export instructions and MuseDraw’s diagram gallery. Core export tools alone are not an AI workflow without a documented learned authoring stage.
Completed local generation, restoration and relighting guides and revisited capture research. Synthesized detail must not be confused with measured scene information.
Read QGIS AI Agent’s plan/apply and data-sharing disclosures and screened structured board authoring. Generated spatial or conceptual diagrams still need a factual check.

Completed AI-assisted LED pattern authoring and stage detection guides; revisited projection and biosignal installation contexts. Photos, equipment and site-specific calibration require separate review.

Reviewed gesture instruments, learned audio wrapping and AI stage tracking. OpenFollow’s optional AI path is explicitly experimental; the label is scoped to that route. Further metadata review found AI shader authoring in Hallucinate and a neural camera-depth layer in CLAP Visualizer; ordinary beat/frequency analysis is labeled separately.
Read the INTEX textile-design case study. It describes AI-assisted material selection and sustainability goals, not proof of a newly installable open-source garment-design application.

Reviewed speech transcription, comic translation and GitLab dubbing work. Weeablind’s source tree did not establish a complete software license, so its accessibility intent alone did not qualify it for inclusion.
Read SDAI’s F-Droid listing and immersive-web development material. The listing distinguishes Android local engines from iOS remote generation; device and model compatibility remain specific.
Read the creative-ML curriculum and MIT learning playground, and completed an explainer-video guide. Educational content licenses and software licenses are not interchangeable.
Read PyPottery’s documentation pipeline and reviewed score/audio candidates. Recognition and reconstruction outputs need comparison with the original artifacts.

Added landscape design and mosaic art before collection, and revisited scent, haptics and folding research. Research pages without a complete reviewed software grant remain findings rather than eligible additions.
Read HapticGen’s text-conditioned vibration workflow and evaluation description. Its authors’ study is not our own device test, and peripheral compatibility needs separate evidence.
Read learned acoustic-field examples alongside geometry-based simulation. Only an identified learned contribution supports AI eligibility.

Reviewed editable film, node-workspace and procedural-scene contexts; screened adapters for pixel art, 3ds Max and show control. External agents and proprietary hosts remain explicit. Choreon provides an editable shot pipeline with local rendering and external agents; provider costs, imported content and execution permissions need operator review.
Read modal typography research and screened motion-pack’s agent-driven authoring workflow. A forthcoming research code release is not counted as available software.
Revisited graph-based dance generation and contextual motion synthesis. Lighting choreography candidates without a clear license remain outside today’s featured entries.
Reviewed textile material selection and folding research. A generative geometry algorithm is not automatically AI, and digital plausibility is not fabrication validation.
Revisited binary piano-roll generation and inspected a string-quartet OMR benchmark repository. The latter lacked a complete root software grant in this pass and was held for clarification.

Completed SyncLight’s guide and read its checkpoint card alongside Lumen’s video overview. The direct SyncLight site fetch had a certificate error; the research browser provided readable primary text.
Read Anemoia and the updated AromaGen abstract. The reviewed material did not establish a new complete licensed application release; scent composition is not a safety validation.
Read instruction-driven indoor layout, procedural assembly and garden-scene research. These are digital scene workflows, not validated building or planting plans.
Read DirectL and Princeton’s neural point light-field descriptions. A learned view representation and a calibrated physical multi-view display are separate requirements.
Revisited contextual motion and performer-tracking material. Foton’s landing page returned only a title and did not establish a new implemented AI puppetry workflow.
Read PyPottery’s extraction, vectorization and publication pipeline. Digital documentation does not establish clay, firing or glazing suitability.
Completed KimCad’s guide and revisited procedural CAD. Its explicit beta and mock-printer limits are visible; model-generated parameters require dimensional review.
Read the QGIS plugin registry’s current agent behavior and remote-data disclosures. No map was modified or private project transmitted during research.
Read FRIDA’s learned stroke simulation and feedback-driven planning. Demonstrations do not validate an arbitrary robot, brush, paint or work area.
The ToonComposer fetch again supplied only a title. Adjacent animation research was readable, and sprite/stickman workflows were screened from their source documentation.
Read LTX’s Foley instructions and screened electroacoustic sound generation. The official guide validates its LoRA on LTX-2.3 and says LTX-2.5 support remains in development.

Read CoolChic’s current setup and LenslessMic’s learned optical/audio reconstruction examples, plus self-similarity compression research. No security-equivalence or audio-fidelity claim was independently validated.
Reviewed learned music similarity and neural sound-object exploration. AudioStellar’s GitLab HTML pages returned loading shells today; no unchanged guide was repeated from those fetches.
Read Timeflux and MindDrawPlay and screened EEG-to-audio generation. Artistic mapping of physiological signals is not verified thought decoding.
Read Material Apprentice’s editable Blender-graph workflow and reviewed learned mosaic/texture synthesis. Editable shader programs still require renderer and parameter checks.
Read event-to-video and lensless-camera reconstruction material. Hardware acquisition, calibration and real-world reconstruction quality were not tested.
Revisited COrigami’s flat-foldable design paper. A clear released software grant was not established, so it remains a research finding rather than a featured app.

New effective field: searched garden, terrain and landscape design. GardenDesigner describes agent-built Unity scenes, but its retrieved repository did not provide a complete software license; Landkit and Landscape Generation also remain held.

New effective field: completed licensed diffusion-tile, adversarial-mosaic and semantic-collage guides, and screened neural fractal representations. Model Mosaic’s README says MIT but its actual file uses a custom license; it was held.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Read Weeablind’s source README and root tree through the public API. Its creative dubbing route is concrete, but no complete license was retrieved. AudioStellar HTML pages returned loading shells. This bounded pass did not establish a new eligible GitLab addition.

Inspected live public search results: zero AI-art matches and a bounded first 50 diffusion matches, including non-AI scientific diffusion and mirrors. Read Imaginer’s current README, license and build metadata; it remains an earlier screened entry. Read the RAVE latent-diffusion app README and license: its application is CC BY-NC-SA, so it is excluded from open-source additions.

Read four neural-search results and the first audio-results page (15 entries, page 1 of 4). These included generic ML lessons and conventional audio tools; none established a new licensed creative AI addition in this bounded review. The existing Diffuser landing page was also checked.

Read fresh PyPI JSON metadata for Neutone SDK and Artefex and the SDAI F-Droid listing. Read-only inspection of the Neutone 1.5.2 wheel confirmed that its complete LGPL-2.1 license matches the repository despite a conflicting metadata classifier; nothing was installed or run. A challenge page on vak did not count as package evidence; its direct documentation was readable. Registry metadata does not prove quality.
Read the official Neutone FX model-host page and QGIS registry, and screened Aseprite, 3ds Max and BEYOND integrations. Required host products and model services are disclosed separately.

Read current primary pages across all effective creative fields, including garden synthesis and neural collage. Shell-only pages and the initial SyncLight certificate failure are disclosed rather than counted as substantive source reads.

Followed official project pages into source repositories for neural collage, mosaics, relighting and scene evaluation. Full software grants, model/data restrictions and implementation availability were checked separately.

Read Korean comic-translation documentation, Chinese gesture/stickman guides, French/English Mac image-generation context and German textile research. Language and popularity did not determine eligibility or quality confidence.
